published_parameter_notes: The intake subsection gives crowding c=100, whereas the paper's final standard-configuration paragraph gives c=200. Use and identify the chosen configuration rather than treating the text as unambiguous.

Published plant production is 0.015 * (0.065 * total NPP + belowground fraction * grass NPP). The belowground fraction is max(0.2, (88.3 - 0.0534 * annual precipitation mm) / 100). NPP must be in dry-matter units consistent with the food pools.

Original accessible prey stock uses an independently simulated grazer/browser density, a 180 kg live animal, accessible fraction 0.1 and live-to-edible-dry-mass fraction 0.28. The atlas adapter has no such herbivore simulation.
Original population floor is a numerical reinoculation, not evidence of actual habitation. Empty or failing habitats must not be advertised as populated by that floor.
Food density is kg dry matter per m2. Human density is persons per km2 and must be divided by one million when constructing human biomass and removing food.

adapter_assumptions.npp: The existing Miami estimate is annual g dry matter per m2 per year. Multiplication by 1000 converts it to kg dry matter per km2 for the kernel; equivalently divide by 1000 for kg per m2, then multiply by one million m2 per km2. Normalized seasonal weights preserve annual input, but do not reconstruct daily photosynthesis, ORCHIDEE allocation or weather variability.
adapter_assumptions.grass_npp_fraction: A globally fixed 0.5 is an uncalibrated mixed-vegetation scenario. It is not a biome-specific grass-cover observation. No arbitrary biome-to-density ranking is introduced.
adapter_assumptions.plant_decay_day: A fixed daily loss fraction of 0.02 is an uncalibrated food-resource turnover scenario. It is not a published universal FORGE parameter and is not harvested-food storage or technological preservation.
adapter_assumptions.annual_meat_fraction_of_npp: A globally fixed 0.0005 of annual dry-matter NPP supplies an illustrative accessible prey budget. It replaces missing grazer/browser and trophic dynamics, has not been calibrated against herbivore or human observations, and does not reproduce the published accessible-animal fraction by itself.
adapter_assumptions.annual_prey_stock: The proxy prey budget is supplied once at the start of the year; hunting depletes it. Residual prey is discarded and separately accounted before annual replacement. There is no hidden daily recruitment. This schedule is inspired by FORGE's annual stock update, but omits animal births, mortality and feedback from human hunting.
adapter_assumptions.phenology: Temperature floor/span and rainfall half-saturation are transparent uncalibrated seasonal resource proxies. When all seasonal weights vanish, use a documented uniform fallback while retaining the annual NPP budget; do not manufacture an observed growing season.
adapter_assumptions.land_use: Treat this as a separate wild-food counterfactual. Do not add its full-land potential to full-land crop or pasture support, which would allocate the same land and primary production more than once.

limitations: No reproduced ORCHIDEE vegetation, plant functional types, soil carbon, grazer/browser demography or original global FORGE calibration.
Monthly mean climate cannot resolve daily weather or resource covariance. Any daily timing is a scenario interpolation.

No small game, migration, trade, food sharing between cells, institutions or crop production is represented by these foraging maps. Fish and other aquatic foods enter as one coastal and freshwater supply (aquatic block), fitted on North American foragers and tested on the rest of the world; seasonal fish runs and food storage are not represented.
Environmental pathogen exposure is not inferred from meat or foraging effort. The Tallavaara empirical pathogen predictor is not the atlas malaria index.
Foraging density and effort concern subsistence under stated resources. They do not predict surplus appropriation, social complexity, innovation or political development.
Alternative resource parameters are sensitivity scenarios, not calibrated probabilities or statistical confidence intervals.
model_note: Independent implementation of published FORGE human energy, effort and demographic equations with an explicitly simplified resource adapter. It is not the original ORCHIDEE-FORGE simulation, an agricultural carrying capacity, a c.200 AD census or a ranking of societal development. Terrestrial food is scaled by 0.5 and coastal and freshwater fish are a third food stock, both fitted on Binford's North American hunter-gatherers and tested on the rest of the world (reports/FORAGING_EARTH_20261031.md).
run_note: Finite maximum of 300 simulated years; density, effort, diet and scarcity summaries use up to the final 50 annual cycles. Annual-state convergence is a separate explicit check; a cycle-averaged scenario is not declared equilibrium when that check fails. Initial density and the stopping rule are implementation settings, not a replication of the original global initialization.

implementation_units.daily_food_supply: kg dry matter per km2 per day
implementation_units.area_conversion: 1 g dry matter per m2 = 1000 kg dry matter per km2; search area converts m2 to km2 internally

aquatic.map_river_scale_note: The map draws rivers in more detail than Natural Earth 1:10m: 0.73 against 0.418 km per 100 km2 of land (both classes of the drawing against Natural Earth on Earth), so map river length is scaled by 0.418/0.73 before the freshwater index is formed. Fixed from the two datasets before any atlas result.
aquatic.map_sst_note: The atlas climate packet carries land values over the sea (coastal fill), so the map uses the model's zonal sea surface (energy-balance ocean column plus sst_offset) at each cell's latitude, annual mean. Deviation from the addendum, recorded.
aquatic.supply: a_marine * exp(-d_coast/coast_scale_km) * clip((sst_zero_c - SST)/sst_span_c, sst_floor, 1) + a_fresh * W_fresh, kg dry matter per km2 of land per year, spread evenly over the year; W_fresh = river and lake-centre line length within radius_km in km per 100 km2 + lake_weight x lake-covered share of that disc
